name: agent-fs-tool-suite
body:
The agent filesystem tool suite: the three new suite tools `apg_rm`, `apg_mv`, `apg_cp` (planned files `opencode-suite/tools/apg_rm.ts`, `opencode-suite/tools/apg_mv.ts`, `opencode-suite/tools/apg_cp.ts` — declared as planned Implementation nodes by the plan-writer) plus the shared `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` plumbing they reuse and extend. Each tool takes the caller's project `directory` plus the operation's path(s), resolves them against the project root via the existing `findApgRoot` / `resolveProjectPath` boundary, performs a plain filesystem operation, and SELF-ENFORCES scope: it refuses a path that escapes the project/worktree boundary AND a path not matched by the acting agent's granted globs (read from the caller's agent permission block via the opencode plugin context; how the acting agent is discovered is an implementation concern for the plan, not a spec open question). The shared lib holds the single-sourced path-resolution/containment/permission-scope helpers the three tools call (DRY per `global.constraint.decomposition-quality`). The tools are product source embedded via `include_str!` and installed by `apg init` (see `solution.component.agent-fs-install-registry`), per `solution.constraint.suite-is-product-source`; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and are never edited by this change-set.

implemented-by: `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` (the shared plumbing the tools extend). The three tool files are planned — their FQNs (`opencode-suite/tools/apg_rm.ts`, `opencode-suite/tools/apg_mv.ts`, `opencode-suite/tools/apg_cp.ts`) are declared by the plan-writer and become implemented-by targets once they exist.
